premise: A former gunslinger turned reluctant marshal must face the outlaw gang he once ran with, led by his own brother.
setting: The high-desert town of Redoubt, 1881: a saloon, a failing telegraph office, badlands all around.
greeting: Rosa's hand was already on the shotgun when the stagecoach bell clattered through the dust — Marshal Callan's signal, two hours early, and the look on the boy's face said it wasn't good news.

name1.name: Marshal Callan
name1.description: A quiet marshal trying to bury a violent past; slow to anger, fast when moved.

name2.name: Rosa
name2.description: The saloon's sharp-eyed owner who knows everyone's secrets and keeps the town's ledgers.

writing_style.directive: Lean Western plainness. Sparse dialogue, weather and dust as texture. One clean beat per turn. Dual close-third-person narration: Callan and Rosa are each narrated from inside their own spare restraint.
writing_style.guide_directive: Third-person past tense in close narration on Marshal Callan — 'he' is always Callan; record what a man says, drinks, and does not feel. Flat, spare, unsentimental; dust-dry declaratives, weather as mood.
writing_style.dss_directive: Third-person past tense in close narration on Rosa, the saloon owner — 'she' is ALWAYS Rosa; Callan is 'he'. Economical and shrewd from the outside — her bar, her ledger, her loyalties. Lean plain prose, weather and dust as texture. Hard rules: keep the third person — never slip into 'I' for Rosa; never quote or repeat Marshal Callan's lines back verbatim — respond to them, do not re-speak them; end on action or observation, not summary.

notes.content: Callan's coat has a button engraved USM — a U.S. Marshal button he does not explain. Rosa notices it and says nothing.
Rosa's shotgun, which the town calls Old Faithful, sits behind the bar with its action oiled and ready.
Callan always pays for his whiskey in exact change, and never takes change back.
The telegraph operator Jonas Fenn is deaf in his left ear from a key that backfired ten years ago.
A burned stagecoach stop on the north road, fresh ash still smoking, the first sign of something moving toward Redoubt.
Callan's hat has a hole in the brim where a rattlesnake bit him, and he keeps wearing it.
Rosa has a scar across the web of her left hand from a knife she threw at a man who touched her daughter.
The blacksmith in town makes his living sharpening scythes for the ranches, not guns, and seems proud of it.
Callan sleeps with a knife under his pillow, a habit he has not broken since the old days with the gang.
A stranger in a faded duster passes through town early one morning asking for directions to the Fitch ranch.
Rosa's ledger has entries in two different hands, and she does not explain who the other hand belongs to.
The doctor in town is old and slow, and his remedies are mostly prayer and cheap whiskey from Rosa's stock.
Callan's horse has a habit of backing up stiff-legged when it hears a dog bark, and Callan never chides it for it.
A boy from the Fitch ranch arrives at the saloon with news of trouble on the north road, men with rifles.
Rosa's best customer is a traveling peddler with a wagon of buttons and thread who never says where he comes from.
Callan's boots are worn through at the heels, and he refuses to buy new ones even though Rosa offers to front the money.
The minister's daughter carries a Bible with her everywhere but has never been seen to open it.
A telegram arrives at the telegraph office: a wanted poster for Silas Callan has been issued by the Territorial Governor in Santa Fe.
Jonas Fenn taps out a long message one night, holds it, and then tears it up, feeding the paper into the stove.
Rosa's daughter left Redoubt two years ago and has never written back, and Rosa does not talk about it.
The saloon's pianist is blind but remembers every song he has ever played, including ones no one in town has heard in years.
needle_syns: the blind man at the piano

notes.content: Two men from out of town buy up all the rope from the general store, paying in silver coins.
Callan has a small cedar box containing letters he wrote but never sent, which he keeps in his saddlebag.
Rosa's father was Redoubt's first marshal and was killed by a man he was escorting to the county seat.
The general store owner sells guns but only to men who can produce a written order from a sheriff.
A fresh boot print is found in the dust of the saloon's back room that does not match any man in town.
Callan's revolver has a custom grip carved from cow bone, with a pattern he carved himself in the old days.
Rosa keeps a collection of foreign coins in a drawer behind the register, coins from places the town has never seen.
In a newspaper from Denver, Callan sees a photo of Silas's gang — and recognizes the cow-bone grip on his own revolver in the hands of the second man from the left.
The town's lawyer is actually a fugitive from a debt collectors' court in Denver, pretending to be an attorney.
Rosa's son-in-law rides for the railroad and brings news from outside town once a month, always in the same dark suit.
A herd of cattle crosses the badlands at night, heading slowly toward the Fitch ranch, and Callan watches them go.
When Callan is angry, his left hand shakes slightly, and he hides it by putting it in his pocket.
The blind pianist was a preacher in another state before he lost his sight, and he still hums hymns while he plays.
The wanted poster for Silas Callan arrives by stage and is nailed to the wall of the saloon, and everyone in town reads it.
Behind the saloon's kitchen there is a small locked room that Rosa keeps the key to on her person, and no one has seen inside it in years.
Callan's horse knows the route to the Fitch ranch, even though Callan has never told him where it is.
Jonas Fenn keeps a small leather-bound code book under the telegraph key, and he closes it when anyone enters the office.
Three men from the Fitch ranch who were out checking fences have not come back, and their horses are tied up at the saloon.
In Rosa's ledger, there is an entry for a payment of forty dollars from one marked only S.C., dated three weeks ago.
On Callan's right forearm, half-hidden by his sleeve, is a cattle brand mark from a drive he worked twenty years ago.
When Rosa mentions the wanted poster, Callan unconsciously touches the USM button on his coat, a habit he did not know he had.

recall.hint: Callan touches the USM button reflexively when the poster is mentioned

notes.content: The S.C. payment in Rosa's ledger is from Silas Callan, who rode through town three weeks ago as a stranger asking for directions to the Fitch ranch.

recall.hint: Rosa realizes the S.C. payment was Silas

notes.content: The stranger who asked for directions to the Fitch ranch had a limp in his right leg, the same limp Callan remembers from his boyhood.
Callan recognizes the description of the stranger as his brother Silas, the man he thought was dead in New Mexico.
The Fitch ranch becomes the focal point of the town's fear; no one goes there anymore, and the lights are visible at night.
Rosa finds a .45 shell casing behind the saloon bar, a caliber Silas carries that almost no one else does.
In Callan's cedar box of unsent letters, there is one addressed to Silas, written years ago, that he never had the courage to send.
Callan realizes that the Fitch ranch is where Silas has been hiding, running his gang operations from a place the town never thought to look.
Rosa tells Callan, for the first time, that her daughter was taken by Silas's gang two years ago, which is why she left.
The USM button on Callan's coat is not a U.S. Marshal button at all — it is a mark of Silas's gang, a signal between members.

recall.hint: The USM button is revealed to be a gang signal

notes.content: The stranger at the Fitch ranch asks to buy the general store's entire stock of dynamite, paying in gold.
Jonas Fenn's code book uses the same cipher that Silas's gang uses for their messages, and Jonas has been tapping out their traffic all along.
The telegraph line is cut, and no word can go out from Redoubt; the town is sealed in.
When Rosa tells Callan about her daughter, his shaking hand stops; for the first time in weeks it is steady.

recall.hint: Callan's shaking hand steadies when he learns about Rosa's daughter

notes.content: Inside Rosa's secret locked room there is her father's old marshal badge, tarnished but clean, sitting in a box on a shelf.
The wanted poster is torn down from the saloon wall and burned in the woodstove, and no one protests.

recall.hint: The wanted poster is taken down and destroyed

notes.content: A boy from the north road says that at night the Fitch ranch is burning bright, like they are forging something.
Callan decides, at the saloon bar, that he will not leave town; he will face Silas wherever he is.
Rosa takes her father's marshal badge from its box and pins it to her jacket, and joins Callan on the porch.

recall.hint: Rosa puts on her father's badge and stands with Callan

notes.content: Silas's plan is revealed: he intends to dynamite the railroad grade south of town and reroute all traffic through Redoubt, making the town his.
The railroad rider confirms that there are more than ten men at the Fitch ranch, armed and dug in.
